Migration is complete. All JavaScript files pass `node --check`.

**Changed (12 files, 36 call sites):**
- `packages\accounts\src\repo\session.js`, `packages\accounts\src\admin\apiKeyAdmin.js`, `packages\accounts\src\service\teamService.js`
- `packages\analytics\src\repo\cohort.js`
- `packages\billing\src\repo\refund.js`, `packages\billing\src\service\couponService.js`
- `packages\catalog\src\repo\supplier.js`, `packages\catalog\src\admin\variantAdmin.js`
- `packages\orders\src\repo\shipment.js`, `packages\orders\src\service\returnService.js`
- `packages\support\src\repo\sla.js`, `packages\support\src\admin\macroAdmin.js`

Each call moved from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`. The SQL text and the parameter arrays are unchanged, so behaviour is the same.

**Not changed — two items you must decide on:**

1. `vendor\legacy-orm\adapter.js:9` and `:13` still call `db.query`. The file header says that it is a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, and that local edits are lost on every upgrade. I left it alone. To remove the last callers, you must patch the vendor package upstream, or wrap the adapter in first-party code.
2. `cache.query(...)` calls in many repo files are a different object (`lib/cache.js`). They are not part of this migration.

`db.query` is still defined in `lib/db.js`. You can delete it after the vendor file moves over.
